$why: Not a prompt — no model receives it. It is the commit message the health check writes when an
agent produced files and did not commit them, and it is PROSE: a human reads it in git log,
months later, trying to work out why a commit exists that no agent claims.
Text a person reads belongs in the template layer for the same reason a prompt does. As a
heredoc it could not be reviewed, diffed against the other things the engine says, or changed
without editing a shell script — and the attribution line at the bottom had gone stale where
description: The commit message written when an agent leaves its output uncommitted.
body:
chore(wt-__LANE__): auto-commit agent output for phase __PHASE__

Automated commit of __CHANGED_COUNT__ file(s) produced by the __LANE__ agent.
Phase: __PHASE__
Lane: __LANE__
Timestamp: __TIMESTAMP__

WARNING: this was auto-committed by worktree-health-check.sh because the agent
did not commit its own changes. Review these files.

Co-Authored-By: __AUTHOR__
